scope: Delta only. Phase 8C.1 rotated the local credentials, moved the stack onto a round-specific volume, and added graceful shutdown to the backend process. Everything docker-stack-v1.json records that 8C.1 did not touch still stands; the items listed as superseded below do not.

unchanged_from_v1.backend_image_shape: golang:1.24.10 -> scratch, non-root 65532:65532, no host port, rootfs entries 16
unchanged_from_v1.frontend_image_shape: node:22 build -> nginx:1.27-alpine serving dist only, rootfs entries 2216
unchanged_from_v1.internal_data_network: gopherlearn-app-data stays internal: true; the frontend still cannot reach MySQL's container address

credentials.why: docker-stack-v1.json records that the previous values had once appeared in a `docker compose config` invocation without --no-env-resolution. They are rotated rather than argued about.
credentials.method: Generated from /dev/urandom and written with in-place field edits, so no value was ever printed to a terminal, a log, an artifact or a tool transcript. The example file and the variable names are unchanged.
credentials.git_ignored: matched by the *.local rule; `git check-ignore -v` reports .gitignore:2
credentials.rotation_caveat: Changing .env.compose.local does not change the passwords MySQL stored in an already initialised data directory. Pointing new credentials at the old volume therefore fails in a way that looks like a broken stack. 8C.1 starts from a fresh volume instead of running ALTER USER against the old one.

volumes.previous_round_volume: gopherlearn-8c-mysql-data (retained, not mounted by this round, not deleted)

graceful_shutdown.mechanism: signal.NotifyContext for SIGINT and SIGTERM is installed before anything is opened; serveUntil runs Serve in a goroutine and on cancellation calls http.Server.Shutdown with a deadline of shutdownGrace, then Close if the deadline fires.
graceful_shutdown.ordering_guarantee: Shutdown closes the listener first, so a request arriving after the signal is refused instead of being queued and served; requests already running keep their connections until they finish or the window expires.
graceful_shutdown.exit_behaviour: The process returns from main, so the container exits 0. A forced close still exits 0 and logs that the drain window was exhausted - a non-zero code there would tell a supervisor to keep restarting a process that was asked to leave.
graceful_shutdown.semantics_unchanged: No retry was added, no readiness or health route was added, no Redis or RabbitMQ was introduced, and request, auth, learning, RAG, agent and memory behaviour is untouched: the HTTP contract golden did not move by one byte.
graceful_shutdown.supersedes_v1_limitation: docker-stack-v1.json's shutdown_observations recorded that main.go had no signal handling and that `docker stop` ended the process with exit code 2, and its limitations listed the same fact. Both are closed by this round. The observation about go-sql-driver's `closing bad idle connection: EOF` during a graceful MySQL restart is unchanged and still stands.

docker_stop_with_24_parallel_streams_in_.correlation_note: The stop was issued two seconds into the workload, so the slower streams were genuinely mid-flight when the signal arrived; the fastest ones may already have finished. The claim is bounded accordingly: streams still running at the signal reached their terminal event.

measured.requests_arriving_while_stopped: 504 from Nginx, not 200 - nothing new was served while the backend was gone
measured.windows_signal_test: The pure-Go SIGTERM case skips on Windows with a reason rather than passing vacuously; the loopback drain tests and this Docker measurement are what carry the claim on this host.

browser_core_flow_under_new_credentials.stale_token_after_secret_rotation: The token signed with the previous JWT secret is rejected, and the SPA bounced to /login and cleared the stored auth on its own.

gates.go_build: host, GOOS=linux and GOOS=windows all build (syscall.SIGTERM compiles on Windows)
gates.mysql_gated_integration_suite: 250 PASS lines / 0 FAIL against the 8C.1 volume's MySQL 8.0.46
gates.docker_compose_config_no_env_resolution: exit 0, stop_grace_period and the round-specific volume present

mutation_probe.change: server.Shutdown(drain) replaced by server.Close(), single anchor
mutation_probe.result: all three stop-path tests fail, each for its own reason: the in-flight stream is cut with an unexpected EOF, the drained-stream assertion fails, and the forced-close case returns nil where errShutdownForced is required
mutation_probe.first_attempt_rejected: An earlier variant of this mutation failed to compile instead of failing a test (removing the only use of `drain`), which is reported rather than hidden because a mutation that never ran proves nothing

not_claimed: Graceful shutdown is not zero-downtime. A stream slower than the drain window is still cut, and there is still no retry, because replaying a request whose outcome is unknown turns one possible success into two possible side effects.
The SSE buffered-versus-passthrough question remains unanswered on this host; 8C.1 did not improve the measurement, and docker-stack-v1.json's why_not still applies.
This stack remains a single-machine development setup: one replica per service, no Redis, no RabbitMQ, no real provider.
No message body, document text, account identifier, password, DSN, JWT or token is recorded in this file.
